inputs.prompt:
<Picture 1> is the authoritative spatial map of the world, not a visual-style reference. Treat it as a top-down geometric specification of a Yuanmingyuan-style imperial garden park in Beijing: tree-lined gravel paths, a big ornamental lake with lotus leaves, white-marble ruins blocks of the Western Mansions, stone balustrades, a narrow stone causeway, Chinese pavilions in the distance, summer daylight. Do not imitate the appearance of the map; infer plausible 3D terrain and architecture.

FIRST-PERSON BICYCLE CAMERA, non-negotiable: shot from a camera mounted on the bicycle's handlebar at exactly 1.6 meters above the ground, looking straight ahead horizontally. The handlebar grips and both of the rider's hands holding them are ALWAYS VISIBLE at the bottom edge of the frame, in every frame. The ground surface fills the lower half of the frame; trees and balustrades pass at eye level; the horizon stays near the middle. The camera NEVER rises above 1.6 m. Absolutely NO aerial view, NO drone shot, NO bird's-eye view, NO top-down view.

ONE CONTINUOUS RIDE, no stopping anywhere (total 10.0 seconds, 24 fps):
- 0.0s-3.5s: ride straight north along the tree-lined gravel path at steady cycling speed; the lake with lotus leaves is on your LEFT at eye level.
- 3.5s-6.5s: reach the stone plaza junction and, WITHOUT slowing down, bend the path into a smooth continuous LEFT arc of 90 degrees onto the stone causeway that crosses the lake. The turn happens WHILE MOVING, like a real cyclist leaning into a bend; the view sweeps smoothly to the left.
- 6.5s-10.0s: now riding straight along the causeway at the same steady speed; white stone balustrades on both sides at hand height; lotus-covered lake water on BOTH sides; a small gate pavilion at the far end grows closer. The clip CUTS while still moving at full speed toward the gate — do NOT slow down, do NOT arrive.
The full continuous-motion LEFT turn onto the causeway is the single most important goal: heading at 10.0s must be 90 degrees left of the heading at 0s.
